chapter: Hampton and Basie: tours and road life
title: Jazz respected abroad, undervalued in America
summary: Royal argues jazz is America's own culture yet musicians are least valued at home.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: That's right. That's the way they think about you. They love you. You're respected. Jazz, in every country except the United States, is put on a pedestal. Jazz

players are respected. They're loved and they're wanted. Over here, the person that's a jazz aficionado, they get so much free and they're accepted as something that just happened, because this is where it came from; this is the roots. Jazz is the only American culture that there is that can actually stand on its own feet and say that it didn't come from the mother country.

The next thing to that is country and western and even that is derived from a lot of the European types of songs and things, where the cowboys sing to their herds the way that the shepherds and things sang to their herds in the old country. Those are the only two types of original culture that the United States has. Everything else came from the fatherland or some other land.
But over here, a musician is less thought of than anyplace in the world.
Whether it does or not, that's the way it stands and that's my observation. I say that with a straight face. I'm unbiased and uncallused in any way. It's the honest to God's truth.
